title: Resolve fractional attribution & hourly-smearing in per-model console charts due to rate-limited streaming truncation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Console per-model breakdown charts are showing a persistent 'smearing' of tokens across hourly buckets and small fractional token totals attributed to model variants. Root symptoms: (1) hourly spikes followed by negative adjustments in later backfilled windows, (2) small fractional token rows in per-model tables (e.g., 0.3 tokens), and (3) customer-reported inconsistencies between raw usage events and Console totals after a rate-limit surge on 2026-02-27.
root_cause: Preliminary investigation shows combination of three interacting issues: streaming request truncation during rate-limit enforcement emits partial tokenized events without deterministic lineage IDs; the ingestion pipeline normalizes timestamps by ingest_time for first pass then later replays use event_time leading to bucket mismatch; and the meterer attempts to fractionally apportion tokens across multiple model variants when request fallback occurs (variant selection + retry path), producing non-integer attribution that's treated differently by realtime counters vs. the backfill job.
investigation_steps: Replayed raw ingestion window 2026-02-27 18:00-20:00 and compared raw stream events to normalized records (storage/stream-debug/2026-02-27.tar.gz)
Inspected rate-limit throttle logic in router service (commit hash a1b2c3d) and confirmed partial-response code path returns truncated 'stream_end' event without lineage_id
Ran reconciliation job (usage-recon/v1) with debug flags to surface token delta per event_id
Validated that backfill job (usage-backfill-legacy) uses ingest_time when reconstructing hourly buckets and overwrites earlier realtime tallies
Queried console aggregates and raw metering ledger; identified ~0.8% of tokens in the window are attributed as fractional across >200 model aliases
proposed_solution: Introduce deterministic token_lineage_id propagated from router through to ingestion and meterer so partial events can be merged deterministically
Change backfill pipeline to canonicalize on event_time with a configurable window grace period and a fixed ordering tie-breaker (token_lineage_id) to prevent double-apply
Stop fractional token apportionment in meterer: adopt explicit truncation+carry logic (integer token buckets + carryover to next successful variant) and mark any carry events for later reconciliation

Add a 'usage-aligner-v2' idempotent reconcile job that deduplicates streaming partials using token_lineage_id and replays corrected deltas into console metrics; run on historical window 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-05
Expose a console flag 'include_backfill_corrections' so customers can opt-in to viewing pre-corrected vs corrected charts during rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy deterministic lineage propagation to router + ingestion in staging and run end-to-end with synthetic rate-limit surge tests (target 2026-03-15)
Phase 2 (reconcile job dry-run): run usage-aligner-v2 in dry-run mode against production S3 slices to validate idempotency and deltas (2026-03-17 to 2026-03-19)
Phase 3 (small-scale backfill): execute reconcile job for single customer org with known discrepancies, monitor dashboards for ~48h (2026-03-20)
Phase 4 (full backfill): run corrected backfill across affected window and enable include_backfill_corrections for all customers; ship console release console-2026.04 (2026-03-24)
Rollback: reconcile job supports dry-run/no-op; lineage propagation is backward compatible (router will emit lineage_id only), revert ingestion consumer if unexpected errors occur
test_plan: Unit tests for token_lineage_id generation and propagation in router and SDK
Integration tests to assert idempotence of usage-aligner-v2 against sample partial events set
Load test replicating rate-limit surge with streaming truncation to validate no new fractional attributions under 2x normal QPS
E2E test: run canary backfill against staging console and compare per-model hourly deltas to baseline
QA checklist for Console PM: verify 'include_backfill_corrections' toggles display and that old vs new totals are clearly labeled
acceptance_criteria: No fractional token values displayed in per-model breakdown tables after reconcile (display rounds to integer and stores carry metadata)
Hourly bucket discrepancies between realtime and backfilled views reduced to <0.1% for the tested window
usage-aligner-v2 runs idempotently with zero net-change in dry-run mode and produces reconciled delta file for final run
Console feature flag exposed and docs updated with rollout guidance (Confluence link provided)
